speaker: Unknown
en: Quick introduction.
zh: 简短介绍一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: My name is Drew Knox.
zh: 我叫 Drew Knox。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm the head of product and design at TESOL.
zh: 我是 TESOL 的产品与设计负责人。

speaker: Unknown
en: TESOL is an agent enablement platform.
zh: TESOL 是一个智能体赋能平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: We help you go from scaling skills to building your own software factory.
zh: 我们帮你从扩展技能到构建你自己的软件工厂。

speaker: Unknown
en: So today I'm going to talk about a few things.
zh: 所以今天我要讲几件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: The core is going to focus on harness engineering, which we see as sort of the new discipline of agentic development, and how you can use it to ladder up to a software factory.
zh: 核心会聚焦在 harness 工程(harness engineering)上，我们把它视为智能体开发的一种新学科，以及你如何利用它逐级攀升到一个软件工厂。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before we get started, a few prerequisites.
zh: 在我们开始之前，有几个前提条件。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a bit of an advanced talk in the sense that if you aren't already using coding agents, what I'm about to walk through is probably not where you want to get started.
zh: 这是一个偏进阶的演讲，意思是如果你还没有在使用编码智能体，我接下来要讲的内容可能不是你该入门的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm sort of assuming that if you're working with coding agents, you're used to having a couple sessions at a time.
zh: 所以我某种程度上假设，如果你正在使用编码智能体，你已经习惯了同时开几个会话。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've gotten to a place where coding agents will, for easy tasks and maybe medium complexity tasks, frequently do the right thing.
zh: 你已经到了一个阶段：对于简单任务和中等复杂度任务，编码智能体经常能做对。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're sort of at the sweet spot for starting to think about harness engineering, starting to think about a software factory.
zh: 你大致处于开始思考 harness 工程、开始思考软件工厂的最佳切入点。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I'm going to say here is not exclusive to that, but that's where you'll get your best results.
zh: 我在这里要说的并不局限于那种情况，但那会是你取得最佳结果的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm going to walk through a few things.
zh: 所以我要讲几个方面的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: First, I want to define software factory and talk a little bit about why you might want to build towards one.
zh: 首先，我想定义一下软件工厂，并稍微谈谈为什么你可能想要朝这个方向构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: Second, we're going to then focus a lot on harness engineering, which is kind of the core practice or skill that you'll use to reach a software factory.
zh: 其次，我们会大量聚焦于 harness 工程，它是你用来达到软件工厂的核心实践或技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll talk about what are going to be the components you work on while you're doing harness engineering.
zh: 我们会谈谈在做 harness 工程时，你要处理的组件有哪些。

speaker: Unknown
en: And finally, I'll walk through how the TESOL product briefly can help you along that journey.
zh: 最后，我会简要讲一下 TESOL 产品如何在那段旅程中帮到你。

speaker: Unknown
en: But most of the topics I'm going to talk through here today work with any stack.
zh: 但我今天要讲的大部分主题适用于任何技术栈。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're mostly techniques.
zh: 它们主要是些技巧。

speaker: Unknown
en: TESOL makes them easy, but they're not exclusive to us.
zh: TESOL 让它们变得容易，但它们并不专属于我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: OK, part one, software factories.
zh: 好，第一部分，软件工厂。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are they?
zh: 它们是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no strict definition.
zh: 没有严格的定义。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm sure you're all probably as frustrated as I am with how quickly terminology changes and migrates in the industry today.
zh: 我相信你们可能都和我一样，对当今行业里术语变化和迁移之快感到沮丧。

speaker: Unknown
en: But roughly speaking, a software factory is any agentic system where all of the end product of what you're building and shipping to users
zh: 但大致来说，软件工厂是任何一种智能体系统，其中你正在构建并交付给用户的所有最终产物

speaker: Unknown
en: is created by agents.
zh: 都是由智能体创建的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And your software engineering teams effectively focus on building the factory.
zh: 而你的软件工程团队实际上专注于构建这个工厂。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they work on making the factory more autonomous, more automated, and raising the quality of what it produces.
zh: 所以他们的工作是让工厂更自主、更自动化，并提升它产出的质量。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll go into each of those terms in just a second.
zh: 我马上会逐一展开这些术语。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's kind of the core idea of a factory, though, is everyone on your team effectively becomes internal tool builders, and then you're building a system that produces your product.
zh: 这就是工厂的核心思想：你团队里的每个人实际上都变成了内部工具构建者，然后你构建一个生产你产品的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I mentioned three key metrics.
zh: 所以我提到了三个关键指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are sort of like the pillars you need to think about when building towards a software factory.
zh: 这些大致就是你在朝软件工厂构建时需要思考的支柱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they sort of go in this order.
zh: 而且它们大致按这个顺序来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So autonomy is effectively how much human intervention do you need to get to the right answer.
zh: 自主性实际上是说，你需要多少人工干预才能得到正确答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how many times you need to correct the code or provide a nudge on how the agent should be building.
zh: 也就是你需要多少次纠正代码，或者在智能体应该如何构建上提供推动。

speaker: Unknown
en: Automation, oh, sorry, I've gotten them flipped here.
zh: 自动化——哦，抱歉，我把它们弄反了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Autonomy is the first one.
zh: 自主性是第一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's how much do you humans have to correct?
zh: 它是你们人类需要纠正多少。

speaker: Unknown
en: Automation is how much can you let them run, right?
zh: 自动化是你能让它们运行多少，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: How much do you need to review or build trust in the solution before you accept it?
zh: 在你接受方案之前，你需要多少审查或建立多少信任？

speaker: Unknown
en: They sound quite similar, but there is a difference.
zh: 它们听起来很相似，但确实有区别。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can have high autonomy in the sense that agents frequently are one-shotting the problems you're giving them, but low automation because you don't trust it yet.
zh: 你可以有高自主性，即智能体经常能一次性解决你给它们的问题，但自动化程度低，因为你还不信任它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you're reviewing all of the code directly.
zh: 于是你直接审查所有的代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: You are manually verifying everything.
zh: 你手动验证一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they are distinct things that obviously have a connection, right?
zh: 所以它们是两个不同的东西，但显然有关联，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to build up autonomy first before you can move to automation.
zh: 你必须先建立起自主性，然后才能转向自动化。

speaker: Unknown
en: The final quality, probably the most self-explanatory, how good is the product that you're actually producing for your users?
zh: 最后是质量，大概最不言自明的：你实际为用户产出的产品有多好？

speaker: Unknown
en: These metrics are like your usual user analytics, your test quality, your test coverage, et cetera.
zh: 这些指标就像你常见的用户分析、测试质量、测试覆盖率等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: As you work towards a factory, you're going to go improving autonomy, then improving automation, all while keeping quality constant.
zh: 在你朝工厂努力的过程中，你会先提升自主性，然后提升自动化，同时保持质量不变。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the sort of payoff at the end, why would you want a software factory, is that ultimately we think you can raise quality once you have a factory.
zh: 然后是最后的回报问题：为什么你会想要一个软件工厂？因为我们最终认为，一旦你拥有了一个工厂，你就可以提升质量。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk about this a bit.
zh: 谈谈这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think most folks look at factories as a way to ship faster.
zh: 我认为大多数人把工厂看作是一种更快交付的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: They'll say, like, oh, yeah, you'll get a little bit of slop, but my god, you'll launch so much more features.
zh: 他们会说，比如，哦，是的，你会得到一点垃圾产出，但天哪，你会发布多得多的功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, the cost of return, the ROI will be worth it.
zh: 比如，回报的成本，ROI 会是值得的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's a very short-term phenomenon, right, as agents are sort of coming online and getting better.
zh: 我认为那是一个非常短期的现象，对吧，因为智能体正在上线并变得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: In reality, yes, you will move to higher velocity with a factory.
zh: 实际上，是的，有了工厂你会达到更高的速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: But every team has backlogs of bug fixes or improvements that they wish they could be making that they just don't have time to do, or explorations that they wish they were doing.
zh: 但每个团队都有积压的 bug 修复或改进，他们希望自己能做，只是没有时间去做，或者他们希望自己能做的探索。

speaker: Unknown
en: With a software factory, the idea of a backlog kind of goes away.
zh: 有了软件工厂，积压这个概念基本上就消失了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you actually just have much more capacity to work on test quality improvements, architectural refactors.
zh: 所以你实际上有更多的容量去投入到测试质量改进、架构重构上。

speaker: Unknown
en: So at Tesla, we believe that, yes, at first, as you transition, you will want to keep quality constant or maybe like a very small dip, but that the ultimate payoff is you should see better quality in the code that you're producing.
zh: 所以在 Tesla，我们相信，是的，最初在转型时，你会想保持质量不变，或者可能有很小幅度的下降，但最终的回报是你应该会看到你产出的代码有更好的质量。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, it's great for your overall team collaboration styles.
zh: 此外，它对整个团队的协作方式也很有好处。

speaker: Unknown
en: So once you've moved to a software factory, it's much easier for people who aren't in technical roles to contribute ideas.
zh: 所以一旦你迁移到了软件工厂，非技术角色的人贡献想法就变得容易多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's easier to explore more and to have more perspectives coming in and contributing while your engineering team is much more focused on building the underlying system that everyone is using to push features out to your users.
zh: 所以更容易进行更多探索、有更多视角涌入并做出贡献，同时你的工程团队可以更专注于构建每个人都在用来向用户推送功能的底层系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think ultimately it leads to a more dynamic and inclusive development experience.
zh: 所以我认为最终它会带来一个更有活力、更包容的开发体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how do you get to a software factory?
zh: 那么你如何走向一个软件工厂？

speaker: Unknown
en: Harness engineering is a sign of how fast terms evolve.
zh: Harness 工程是技术术语演进速度之快的一个标志。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's also started to be called loop engineering over the last couple of weeks.
zh: 在过去几周里，它也开始被称为 loop 工程。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is really the core discipline that you're going to take to get towards a software factory.
zh: 这真的是你要走向软件工厂所需掌握的核心学科。

speaker: Unknown
en: At its core, harness engineering is, you know, I mentioned the software factory is building your product.
zh: 从本质上讲，harness 工程是，你知道，我提到过软件工厂是在构建你的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: You are building the loops that automate and improve the quality of your factory.
zh: 而你是在构建那些自动化并提升你工厂质量的循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what do I mean by loops?
zh: 那么我说的循环是什么意思？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the loops that you might be working on?
zh: 你可能正在处理的循环有哪些？

speaker: Unknown
en: There are three core concepts.
zh: 这里有三个核心概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: Each maps to a certain phase of development.
zh: 每一个都对应开发的某个特定阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you have your inner loop.
zh: 首先你有内循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which is as the coding agent is working on a PR before it has put it up.
zh: 也就是编码智能体在一个 PR 提交上去之前处理它时的阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: So these are very fast iterative loops.
zh: 所以这些是非常快速的迭代循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: You want them to be cheap.
zh: 你希望它们是廉价的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're expecting the agent to run them all the time.
zh: 你预期智能体会一直运行它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Improvements here will drive better autonomy.
zh: 这里的改进会带来更好的自主性。

speaker: Unknown
en: They help catch things and correct the agent without your coming in in human intervention.
zh: 它们帮助捕捉问题并纠正智能体，而不需要你进行人工干预。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once the PR is up, you move to the outer loop.
zh: 一旦 PR 提交上去，你就进入外循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is where you're going to put more expensive, exhaustive checks that don't make sense to run over and over again as the agent is iterating on features.
zh: 在这里你会放入更昂贵、更详尽的检查，这些检查在智能体迭代功能时一遍又一遍地运行是没有意义的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But they do encode things that otherwise a human would have to verify to build confidence in the system.
zh: 但它们确实编码了那些原本需要人工验证才能建立对系统信心的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this is because they're more expensive, but they are taking away human review time that can be worth it.
zh: 所以这是因为它们更昂贵，但它们省去了人工审查时间，这可能是值得的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is where you might put something like agentic QA or where you might say like run mutation testing to check the quality of our test suite.
zh: 所以在这里你可能会放入类似智能体 QA 的东西，或者说运行变异测试来检查我们测试套件的质量。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is for expensive things you want to run once when the PR goes up and then have the agent iterate on the results.
zh: 这是为那些昂贵的东西准备的，你想在 PR 提交上去时运行一次，然后让智能体根据结果进行迭代。

speaker: Unknown
en: Finally, you have the meta loop.
zh: 最后，你有元循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is where you'll drive quality.
zh: 这是你驱动质量的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the meta loop sits outside of the development process.
zh: 所以元循环位于开发流程之外。

speaker: Unknown
en: It observes your coding agent logs.
zh: 它观察你的编码智能体日志。

speaker: Unknown
en: It looks at PRs, your issue tracker, user feedback.
zh: 它查看 PR、你的 issue 跟踪器、用户反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's basically finding mistakes that are making their way through the pipeline to your users or that you had to correct as a human to stop that from happening.
zh: 它基本上是在找出那些一路穿过流水线到达你的用户的错误，或者是你不得不作为人类去纠正以阻止其发生的错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it feeds back into the inner and the outer loop to make sure that that mistake is not made again.
zh: 它反馈到内循环和外循环中，以确保那个错误不再被犯。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the outer loop is what really kind of, once you have the infrastructure for each of these loops, the outer loop, or sorry, the meta loop is where you're going to be actually driving from a certain percentage of like how AI native am I, you're going to be driving it up by investing in your meta loop.
zh: 所以外循环才是真正的，一旦你有了这些循环各自的基础设施，外循环，抱歉，元循环才是你真正会从某个百分比——比如我有多 AI 原生——出发，通过投资你的元循环来把这个百分比推上去的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before we get into what are the components, what do you do to actually accomplish this, I think full disclosure up front, harness engineering, at least raw unassisted harness engineering, is hard for a few specific reasons that basically come down to human psychology.
zh: 在我们深入探讨要做什么组件、实际上如何完成这件事之前，我想提前完全坦白，harness 工程，至少是原始的、无辅助的 harness 工程，是很难的，有几个特定的原因，基本上都可以归结为人类心理。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the first, hopefully this one will go away over time, but it's a new discipline and it's changing very fast.
zh: 第一个，希望这个会随着时间消失，就是它是一个新学科，而且变化非常快。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so a lot of teams that get into harness engineering
zh: 所以很多进入 harness 工程的团队

speaker: Unknown
en: You basically become an AI researcher just to try and keep up.
zh: 你基本上变成了一个 AI 研究员，就为了努力跟上。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're reading papers.
zh: 你在读论文。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're watching blogs.
zh: 你在看博客。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're coming up with best practices that go out of date the next week and then two weeks after that.
zh: 你想出一些最佳实践，但下一周就过时了，再过两周又过时了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually, at some point, they become anti-patterns, and you don't want to do them anymore.
zh: 而且实际上，到了某个时候，它们会变成反模式，你不想再用它们了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's just like a lot of time and space you'll devote to keeping up with how to do harness engineering.
zh: 所以你会花费大量时间和空间去跟上如何做 harness 工程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you want to get into this discipline, you need to have a sort of upfront
zh: 因此，如果你想进入这个领域，你需要有一种前置的

speaker: Unknown
en: Approach to how you're going to solve this problem.
zh: 方法来解决这个难题。

speaker: Unknown
en: How are you going to make time and space to keep up with the knowledge that's changing every week?
zh: 你打算如何腾出时间和空间，来跟上每一周都在变化的知识？

speaker: Unknown
en: The second, and this one is more durable in my opinion, harness engineering is fundamentally unplanned work.
zh: 第二点，在我看来这一点更持久，harness 工程本质上是计划外的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you will start shipping a feature.
zh: 所以你会开始交付一个功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have no way to anticipate, will agents fail?
zh: 你没有办法预判，智能体会不会失败？

speaker: Unknown
en: How will they fail?
zh: 会怎么失败？

speaker: Unknown
en: How long is it going to take me to fix it?
zh: 修复它需要我花多长时间？

speaker: Unknown
en: And all of that work that you're going to do to try and make the agent better competes with shipping.
zh: 而你为了让智能体变得更好而做的所有这些工作，都会与交付功能相竞争。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it will slow you down from getting the features out.
zh: 所以它会拖慢你把功能发布出去的速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we all know that is just a perpetually hard trade-off to make.
zh: 而且我们都知道，这是一个永远都很难做的权衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: You either don't do it and you get stuck in the local maxima of the agent never improves, or you do it and you miss your deadline for the feature and you get in trouble and so no one ever does it.
zh: 你要么不做，智能体就永远不会进步，被困在局部最优里；要么做了，就会错过功能的截止日期，惹上麻烦，于是没有人去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: The final piece is that once you've solved these initial problems, things like make time and space for harness engineering, you'll find that a lot of the information you want access to is not available.
zh: 最后一点是，一旦你解决了这些初始问题，比如为 harness 工程腾出时间和空间，你会发现很多你想访问的信息是不可获得的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's hidden away in local coding agent logs, or it is on someone's machine somewhere.
zh: 它们藏在本地编码智能体的日志里，或者在某个人的某台机器上。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's in someone's head.
zh: 它在某个人的脑子里。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of the signals that you want to see to make agents better
zh: 很多你想看到的、用来让智能体变得更好的信号

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to do some work to move your workflows onto surfaces where everything is saved and publicly available for later optimization loops.
zh: 你需要做一些工作，把你的工作流搬到所有内容都会被保存、并且公开可供后续优化循环使用的表面上。

speaker: Unknown
en: With all that aside, then, what are the pieces that you should be working on as you're doing harness engineering?
zh: 把这些放在一边，那么，在你做 harness 工程的时候，你应该着手哪些部分呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: I've broken it into three layers.
zh: 我把它分成了三层。

speaker: Unknown
en: These aren't, by any means, standard terms, though if you want to help me make them so, I would be forever grateful.
zh: 这些绝不是标准术语，不过如果你想帮我把它们变成标准，我会永远感激。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first layer, and these are sort of like in the order you need to do them as far as Tesla is concerned, is you have to get your control plane right.
zh: 第一层，就 Tesla 而言，这些大致是按你需要做的顺序排列的，你必须把你的控制平面弄对。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I mentioned how most of the data that you want to have access to to make agents better and move towards a software factory is not legible.
